neighbours.label: Broad pole; best guess: a preposition marking where something is gone/removed from or moved into ('gone from the island', 'get water into'), after a verb of disappearance or transfer
fire: Without protection these birds would be gone from the valley within a decade.
A pump is needed to get fuel into the engine at a steady rate.
The old customs are now gone from the villages along the coast.
Pipes are needed to get clean water into the houses on the hill.
By morning the snow was gone from the roofs and the streets.
The courtyard can be screened by a row of tall hedges.
It takes pressure to get air into the tyres of a heavy truck.
Wolves have been gone from this forest for almost a century.
quiet: Without protection these birds would be rare in the valley within a decade.
A pump is a simple machine that runs at a steady rate.
The old customs are still alive in the villages along the coast.
The houses on the hill have clean water and good roads.
By morning the snow lay thick on the roofs and the streets.
The courtyard has a row of tall hedges.
A heavy truck has very large tyres.
Wolves have lived in this forest for almost a century.
